name: ESP32 ESP-32S Dev Board (30-Pin)
subtitle: WiFi + Bluetooth Dual-Mode Microcontroller
what_it_does: Powerful dual-core microcontroller with built-in WiFi and Bluetooth for IoT, local web servers, and wireless sensor projects.
visual_tell: Black PCB with a silver ESP-WROOM-32 metal shield can, golden zig-zag WiFi antenna trace at one end, and 2 rows of 15 pins.
warning: 3.3V logic only — do not feed 5V directly into GPIO pins. Hold the BOOT button if flashing fails.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2
subtitle: RP2350 Microcontroller Board
what_it_does: Fast, beginner-friendly microcontroller programmable in MicroPython or C/C++ with programmable I/O (PIO) state machines.
visual_tell: Bright green slim rectangular board with notched castellated edge pads (40 pin holes), black RP2350 chip, and a tiny white BOOTSEL button.
warning: 3.3V GPIO logic. Hold BOOTSEL while plugging in USB to mount it as a drive for flashing.
notes: Requires soldering male pin headers to use on a breadboard.

name: Arduino Uno Clone (SMD CH340)
subtitle: ATmega328P 5V Microcontroller Board
what_it_does: Classic 5V microcontroller board for learning electronics and controlling sensors, motors, and displays via the Arduino IDE.
visual_tell: Blue Uno-shaped PCB with a diamond-rotated square SMD chip, silver USB port, black DC barrel jack, and long black female headers.
warning: Do not confuse with the Breadboard Shield — the Arduino has the USB port and power jack; the shield stacks on top of it.

name: Arduino Uno Super Starter Kit Case
subtitle: Compartmentalized Starter Kit Box
what_it_does: Storage container that originally housed your starter Arduino components and modules.
visual_tell: Translucent plastic compartmentalized box from the Arduino starter kit.

name: 0.91" 128x32 OLED Display (SSD1306)
subtitle: Yellow I2C Mini OLED Screen
what_it_does: High-contrast self-lit miniature screen for displaying sensor readings, status text, or small icons over just 2 data wires (I2C).
visual_tell: Very small narrow dark-blue/black PCB with a glossy black glass screen and only 4 pins (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA) on one narrow side.
warning: Check VCC/GND pin order carefully — some SSD1306 boards swap GND and VCC compared to others.
notes: Default I2C address is typically 0x3C. Works on 3.3V and 5V.

name: 16x2 LCD Display with I2C Module
subtitle: 2-Row Character LCD + I2C Backpack
what_it_does: Displays 2 lines of 16 text characters; the soldered I2C backpack reduces wiring from 12+ pins down to 4.
visual_tell: Green or blue rectangular character screen with a small black I2C adapter board on the back featuring a blue contrast trimmer and 4 pins.
warning: If the screen lights up blank, slowly turn the blue contrast screw on the back backpack until characters appear.
notes: Runs on 5V. Common I2C addresses: 0x27 or 0x3F.

name: 1-Digit 7-Segment Display (5611AH)
subtitle: Common Cathode Single-Digit LED
what_it_does: Lights up individual LED bars to display a single digit (0–9) or simple hex letters.
visual_tell: Small black/grey rectangular block with a single white '8.' digit pattern on front and 10 pins (5 top, 5 bottom).
warning: Do not confuse with the 5641AH (4 digits). Always use current-limiting resistors (e.g., 220Ω) so you do not burn out the segments.
notes: Common Cathode (middle top & bottom pins are GND).

name: 4-Digit 7-Segment Display (5641AH)
subtitle: Common Cathode 4-Digit LED
what_it_does: Displays 4-digit numbers such as clocks, countdown timers, scores, or sensor readings via multiplexing.
visual_tell: Wide black/grey block showing four white '8.8.8.8.' digits side-by-side with 12 pins on the back (6 top, 6 bottom).
warning: Do not confuse with 5611AH (1 digit). Needs current-limiting resistors on the segment pins.
notes: Common Cathode; pairs nicely with the 74HC595N shift register.

name: 8x8 LED Dot Matrix
subtitle: 64-LED Square Matrix Display
what_it_does: Displays scrolling text, mini pixel icons, arrows, or retro animations across 64 addressable row/column LEDs.
visual_tell: Square black/dark-grey block with an 8x8 grid of 64 tiny white circular dots on the front and 16 pins on the back.
warning: Requires current-limiting resistors on rows or columns when driven directly from a microcontroller.

name: 3-Color RGB LED Module (3_CIr)
subtitle: Pre-Resistored RGB Breakout Board
what_it_does: Mixes Red, Green, and Blue light via PWM pins to produce almost any color without needing external resistors.
visual_tell: Tiny black or red PCB with one clear 5mm LED (or flat white SMD LED), 3 tiny SMD resistors, and 4 pins labeled R, G, B, and -.
notes: Connect R, G, B to PWM-capable pins.

name: 5mm LEDs (Yellow, Red, Green)
subtitle: Through-Hole Indicator LEDs
what_it_does: Basic indicator lights for breadboard circuits and status signals.
visual_tell: Classic domed 5mm translucent plastic bulbs with 2 metal legs: longer leg is positive (+), shorter leg next to the flat rim edge is negative (-).
warning: Always pair with a resistor (220Ω–1kΩ) or they will burn out instantly. Do not mix with the dark-tinted LTR-323DB photodetector.

name: Super LED Assortment Pack (118 pcs)
subtitle: Mixed-Color 3mm & 5mm LED Kit
what_it_does: Bulk supply of multi-color indicator LEDs for prototypes and permanent soldered projects.
visual_tell: Assorted pack of red, green, blue, yellow, and white domed LEDs.
warning: Blue and white LEDs have a higher forward voltage (~3.0–3.2V) than red/yellow (~2.0V).

name: DHT11 Temperature & Humidity Sensor Board
subtitle: 3-Pin PCB Breakout Module
what_it_does: Measures ambient temperature (0–50°C) and relative humidity (20–90%) over a single digital data wire.
visual_tell: Light-blue plastic waffle-grid cube mounted on a tiny breakout PCB with 3 header pins (+, OUT/DATA, -) and a built-in pull-up resistor.
warning: Do not confuse with the standalone 4-pin DHT11 — this board already includes the pull-up resistor.
notes: Wait at least 1 second between readings.

name: DHT11 Temperature & Humidity Module
subtitle: Standalone Sensor Element
what_it_does: Measures ambient temperature and relative humidity over a single digital data pin.
visual_tell: Light-blue plastic waffle-grid cube sensor with 4 bare silver pins (or compact 3-pin base).
warning: If using the bare 4-pin version directly on a breadboard, add a 10kΩ pull-up resistor between VCC and DATA.

name: LM35 Precision Temperature Sensor
subtitle: Analog Celsius Sensor (TO-92)
what_it_does: Outputs an analog voltage directly proportional to Celsius temperature (10mV per °C) for accurate temperature readings.
visual_tell: Tiny black half-cylinder (TO-92 package) with 3 thin legs — tilt under light to read 'LM35' engraved on the flat face.
warning: Lookalike alert: looks identical to a standard transistor and similar to the VS1838B IR receiver (LM35 is all black plastic with no metal X-cage). Wiring it backwards heats it up rapidly!
notes: With flat face toward you: Left = VCC (4–30V), Middle = Analog Out, Right = GND.

name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor
subtitle: 2–400cm Sonar Rangefinder
what_it_does: Measures distance to objects (2cm to 400cm) by emitting ultrasonic pulses and timing the returning echo.
visual_tell: Blue rectangular PCB with two large silver mesh cylinders side-by-side ('robot eyes') and 4 pins (VCC, Trig, Echo, GND).
warning: Requires 5V power and outputs a 5V Echo pulse — use a resistor voltage divider on Echo if connecting to a 3.3V ESP32 or Pico 2.

name: MQ-2 Flammable Gas & Smoke Sensor
subtitle: Analog + Digital Gas Sensor Module
what_it_does: Detects LPG, propane, methane, hydrogen, and smoke levels via both an analog reading and a threshold digital output.
visual_tell: Round stainless-steel mesh cylinder mounted on a small blue/green PCB with a blue sensitivity trimpot and 4 pins (VCC, GND, DO, AO).
warning: Contains an internal heater coil — it is normal for the metal mesh to get noticeably warm during operation. Needs 5V and ~1 minute warm-up.

name: HW-038 Water Level Sensor
subtitle: Analog Liquid Depth / Leak Sensor
what_it_does: Detects water contact, leaks, or shallow water depth by measuring conductivity across exposed parallel traces.
visual_tell: Red rectangular PCB with 10 parallel exposed copper/gold vertical stripes on the bottom two-thirds and 3 pins (+, -, S) at the top.
warning: Keep the top electronics area dry. Power it from a digital pin only when reading to slow down copper corrosion.

name: Sound Detection Microphone Module
subtitle: Clap / Noise Threshold Sensor
what_it_does: Detects claps, knocks, or ambient sound spikes; turn the blue potentiometer screw to tune the trigger threshold.
visual_tell: Small red or blue PCB with a round silver microphone cylinder covered in black felt on the front and a blue trimmer box with a brass screw.

name: 5mm LDR (Photoresistor)
subtitle: Light Dependent Resistor
what_it_does: Changes resistance based on ambient light brightness — ideal for automatic night lights or light meters.
visual_tell: Tiny flat round tan ceramic disc with a distinctive reddish-brown wavy zig-zag line across the face and 2 legs (non-polarized).
warning: Pair with a 10kΩ resistor in a voltage divider to read on an analog pin. Do not confuse with the LED-shaped LTR-323DB photodetector.

name: LTR-323DB Photodetector
subtitle: 5mm IR / Optical Photodiode
what_it_does: Fast infrared/optical light detector used for IR break-beam sensors, flame detection, or optical pulse sensing.
visual_tell: Looks almost identical to a dark/black-tinted 5mm LED with 2 legs and a flat rim on the cathode side.
warning: Lookalike alert: looks like a regular 5mm LED, but detects light instead of emitting it! Keep it in its own compartment away from regular LEDs.

name: SW-520D Tilt Sensor
subtitle: Mechanical Ball Tilt / Shake Switch
what_it_does: Simple gravity switch that opens or closes a circuit when tilted past ~15–45° or shaken.
visual_tell: Small black/gold metal cylinder with 2 legs. Gently shake it near your ear — you will hear tiny metal balls rattling inside.
warning: Lookalike alert: resembles a small electrolytic capacitor, but capacitors never rattle when shaken.
notes: Use with INPUT_PULLUP on your microcontroller.

name: VS1838B 38kHz IR Receiver
subtitle: Infrared Remote Signal Decoder
what_it_does: Receives and demodulates 38kHz infrared signals from TV remotes or your mini IR remote control.
visual_tell: Small black 3-legged sensor wrapped in a shiny silver metal X-shaped protective cage framing a black half-sphere dome.
warning: Lookalike alert: do not confuse with LM35 (all-black flat face, no metal X-cage).
notes: Facing the dome: Left = OUT, Middle = GND, Right = VCC (3.3V–5V).

name: Mini Infrared (IR) Remote Control
subtitle: Slim Card-Style 38kHz Remote
what_it_does: Sends wireless infrared button codes to your VS1838B receiver to control projects remotely.
visual_tell: Slim black credit-card-sized remote with round dome buttons (0–9, arrows, OK) and a tiny clear IR LED at the top edge.
warning: Remember to pull out the clear plastic battery-saver tab at the bottom if it has never been used.

name: XY Analog Joystick Module
subtitle: Dual-Axis Thumbstick + Push Button
what_it_does: Reads 2D X/Y movement via two internal potentiometers plus a clickable push button when pressed straight down.
visual_tell: Black concave thumbstick cap on a small square PCB with 5 bent pins on one side (GND, +5V, VRx, VRy, SW).
warning: Enable INPUT_PULLUP on the SW pin for the click button to read reliably.

name: 4x4 Matrix Membrane Keypad
subtitle: 16-Key Flat Sticker Keypad
what_it_does: Allows PIN entry, menu navigation, or calculator input using 8 digital pins (4 rows x 4 columns).
visual_tell: Flat flexible sticker-like pad with 16 colored keys (0–9, A–D, *, #) and an 8-wire flat ribbon ending in an 8-pin female connector.
warning: Do not sharply crease the flat ribbon cable or the printed conductive traces can crack.

name: RC522 RFID/NFC Kit (Reader + Card + Keyfob)
subtitle: 13.56MHz SPI RFID Starter Set
what_it_does: Reads and writes contactless 13.56MHz RFID/NFC tags for smart locks, access control, or interactive triggers.
visual_tell: Blue rectangular PCB with white rectangular spiral antenna traces, bundled with a blank white card and a blue teardrop keyfob.
warning: 3.3V power ONLY! Connecting VCC to 5V will permanently damage the RC522 chip.

name: RC522 RFID Reader (13.56MHz)
subtitle: Standalone SPI RFID Module
what_it_does: Contactless 13.56MHz RFID/NFC reader/writer module communicating over SPI.
visual_tell: Standalone blue rectangular PCB with white spiral antenna traces, a tiny square black chip, and 8 pin holes along one edge.
warning: 3.3V power ONLY — never wire VCC to 5V.

name: Real-Time Clock (RTC) Module
subtitle: Battery-Backed Timekeeping Board
what_it_does: Keeps accurate date and time even when your microcontroller is powered off, using its backup coin-cell battery.
visual_tell: Small blue or black PCB dominated by a round silver coin-cell battery holder and a tiny silver cylindrical crystal oscillator.
warning: If it is a ZS-042 (DS3231) board and you insert a non-rechargeable CR2032, check whether the charging resistor/diode needs disabling.

name: 28BYJ-48 Geared Stepper Motor
subtitle: 5V Unipolar Reduction Stepper
what_it_does: Rotates in precise, countable geared steps for blinds, dials, or slow high-torque positioning.
visual_tell: Round silver metal motor can with two mounting ears, an off-center shaft, a blue plastic wire cover, and 5 colored wires ending in a white 5-pin plug.
warning: Never wire directly to microcontroller pins — always plug into the ULN2003 driver board.
notes: Pairs directly with the ULN2003 driver module.

name: ULN2003 Stepper Motor Driver
subtitle: 4-Phase Darlington Driver Board
what_it_does: Amplifies low-current microcontroller signals to safely drive the 4 coils of the 28BYJ-48 stepper motor.
visual_tell: Small blue/green PCB with a black 16-pin chip, a white 5-pin socket matching the 28BYJ-48 plug, and 4 tiny red LEDs labeled A, B, C, D.
warning: Power the motor's 5V supply cleanly; drawing heavy motor current through a USB port can brown out your microcontroller.

name: SG-90 Micro Servo Motor
subtitle: 9g Plastic-Gear Servo (0–180°)
what_it_does: Moves to a commanded angle (0° to 180°) and holds position — great for latches, pan/tilt mounts, or robotic fingers.
visual_tell: Translucent blue rectangular plastic micro-motor with a white plastic arm horn and a 3-wire flat ribbon (brown, red, orange).
warning: Do not force the horn by hand while powered — the tiny plastic gears strip easily.
notes: Brown = GND, Red = 5V, Orange = PWM Signal.

name: HW-482 1-Channel Relay Module
subtitle: 5V Electromechanical Switch Board
what_it_does: Lets a tiny 5V logic signal switch higher-power circuits (fans, lamps, pumps) on and off with an audible mechanical click.
visual_tell: Small PCB featuring a chunky bright-blue rectangular relay cube and a 3-way green screw terminal block (NO, COM, NC).
warning: Be extremely careful with mains AC voltage — stick to low-voltage DC loads until you are comfortable with mains isolation.

name: Buzzer (5V)
subtitle: Piezo / Magnetic Sounder
what_it_does: Generates beeps, alerts, or simple melodies. Active buzzers beep on steady DC; passive buzzers play tones via PWM/tone().
visual_tell: Small round black plastic cylinder with a center sound hole on top (often marked with a '+') and 2 pins underneath.
warning: Check the underside: a sealed black bottom is usually an active buzzer, while an exposed green PCB underneath is usually passive.

name: 1/4W Metal Film Resistor Kit (600 pcs)
subtitle: 1% Precision 5-Band Assortment
what_it_does: Limits current, divides voltages, and provides pull-up/pull-down resistance across 30+ common ohm values.
visual_tell: Slim light-blue axial resistors with 5 color bands, taped onto labeled paper strips by value.
warning: 5-band metal film color codes are easy to misread backwards — verify with your UT33D+ multimeter in Ω mode whenever in doubt.

name: 220Ω, 1kΩ & 10kΩ Resistors
subtitle: Common Through-Hole Starter Resistors
what_it_does: The three everyday workhorse values: 220Ω protects LEDs, 1kΩ limits signal/base current, and 10kΩ acts as a pull-up/pull-down.
visual_tell: Beige/tan (or blue) axial resistors: Red-Red-Brown = 220Ω, Brown-Black-Red = 1kΩ, Brown-Black-Orange = 10kΩ.
warning: Double-check values with your multimeter if they get mixed loose in a bin.

name: 10kΩ Rotary Potentiometer
subtitle: B10K Linear Variable Resistor
what_it_does: Manual rotary knob acting as an adjustable voltage divider for dimmers, volume, servo angles, or menu scrolling.
visual_tell: Round silver metal base with a knurled vertical shaft and 3 straight pins in a row ('B10K' stamped on the back).
notes: Outer pins to VCC & GND, middle wiper pin to analog input.

name: 74HC595N 8-Bit Shift Register
subtitle: DIP-16 GPIO Expander IC
what_it_does: Expands just 3 microcontroller pins into 8 extra digital outputs — super useful for driving 7-segment displays or LED rows.
visual_tell: Classic black 16-pin rectangular DIP chip (8 legs per side, half-moon Pin 1 notch at one end) with '74HC595N' printed on top.
warning: Always straddle DIP chips across the center ravine of your breadboard so opposing legs do not short together.

name: 12x12mm Tactile Push Button Switch
subtitle: 4-Pin Momentary Switch
what_it_does: Momentary push button that completes a circuit only while held down.
visual_tell: Larger 12x12mm square black switch body with 4 bent metal legs and a round center plunger that clicks.
warning: Pairs of legs are internally bridged — wire diagonally opposite corners to guarantee you never accidentally short the switch closed.
notes: Matches the 12x12mm blue plastic switch caps.

name: 12x12mm Blue Tact Switch Caps
subtitle: Snap-On Button Caps
what_it_does: Snaps onto your 12x12mm tact switches for a larger, more comfortable, color-coded button surface.
visual_tell: Round bright-blue plastic caps with a hollow socket underneath.

name: Full-Size Breadboard (830-Point)
subtitle: Solderless Prototyping Board
what_it_does: Provides a large solderless grid for building and testing multi-component circuits rapidly.
visual_tell: Long white rectangular plastic board (63 rows) with a center ravine and red (+) / blue (-) power rails along both edges.
warning: On some 830-point breadboards, the side power rails have a split break halfway down — check if the colored line has a gap in the middle.

name: Half-Size Breadboard (400-Point)
subtitle: Compact Solderless Breadboard
what_it_does: Medium-sized solderless prototyping board that sits neatly next to an Arduino, ESP32, or Pico 2.
visual_tell: White breadboard roughly half the length of a full board (30 rows), still featuring red/blue side power rails.

name: Red Mini Breadboard (170-Point)
subtitle: Compact Adhesive Mini Breadboard
what_it_does: Ultra-compact solderless block for small sensor tests or sticking onto a project chassis.
visual_tell: Tiny bright-red 17-row breadboard with no side power rails and peel-off adhesive backing.

name: Yellow Mini Breadboard (170-Point)
subtitle: Compact Adhesive Mini Breadboard
what_it_does: Ultra-compact solderless block for isolating a small sub-circuit or snapping onto other mini breadboards.
visual_tell: Tiny bright-yellow 17-row breadboard with interlocking dovetail side tabs and no power rails.

name: Green Mini Breadboard (170-Point)
subtitle: Compact Adhesive Mini Breadboard
what_it_does: Ultra-compact solderless block for standalone sensor or button testing.
visual_tell: Tiny bright-green 17-row breadboard with no power rails and adhesive backing.

name: Arduino Breadboard ProtoShield
subtitle: Stackable Prototyping Shield
what_it_does: Plugs directly on top of your Arduino Uno so a mini breadboard circuit stays attached as one neat unit.
visual_tell: Arduino-shaped shield PCB with a mini white breadboard on top, long stackable pins underneath, and no USB port.
warning: Do not confuse with the Arduino Uno itself — this is the add-on board that plugs onto the Uno's headers.

name: 5x10cm Single-Sided Copper Perfboard
subtitle: Phenolic Prototyping Solder Board
what_it_does: Turns a finished breadboard prototype into a permanent, sturdy soldered circuit.
visual_tell: Tan/brown phenolic board (5x10cm) drilled with a 2.54mm hole grid and shiny copper solder rings on one side only.
warning: Avoid overheating copper pads with your soldering iron — single-sided phenolic pads can lift off if heated for too long.

name: 1x40 Male Pin Header Strip (15mm)
subtitle: 2.54mm Breakaway Straight Headers
what_it_does: Solders onto breakout boards (like Raspberry Pi Pico 2 or RC522) so they plug into breadboards or female jumpers.
visual_tell: Long black plastic comb strip holding 40 straight 15mm metal pins that snap cleanly to any length with side cutters.
warning: Hold the strip over a desk or bag when snapping so the cut piece does not fly across the room.

name: Male-to-Male Jumper Wires
subtitle: Breadboard Hookup Wires
what_it_does: Connects breadboard holes to other breadboard holes or into Arduino female headers.
visual_tell: Rainbow bundle of flexible wires with sharp silver metal pins sticking out of both ends.
warning: Lookalike alert: check both ends so you do not mix them with Female-to-Male jumpers.

name: Female-to-Male Jumper Wires
subtitle: Module-to-Breadboard Hookup Wires
what_it_does: Connects sensor modules with male pins (like HC-SR04 or OLED) directly to a breadboard or Arduino.
visual_tell: Rainbow bundle of wires with a metal pin on one end and a hollow black square socket on the other.
warning: Lookalike alert: one end is a hollow socket, unlike Male-to-Male jumpers.

name: Micro-USB Data Cable (15cm, Black)
subtitle: Short Data + Power Cable
what_it_does: Powers and flashes firmware to your ESP32 and Raspberry Pi Pico 2 cleanly without desk clutter.
visual_tell: Very short (15cm) black USB-A to Micro-USB cable.
warning: Keep these tagged as DATA cables so they never get swapped with charge-only Micro-USB cables.

name: 6x AA Battery Holder
subtitle: 9V Portable Battery Pack
what_it_does: Supplies ~9V portable power (6 x 1.5V) for standalone Arduino projects and motors away from your PC.
visual_tell: Black rectangular plastic case with springs for 6 AA batteries and red (+) / black (-) leads.
warning: Do not feed 9V directly into 3.3V or 5V pins — use the Arduino's VIN / DC barrel jack or a voltage regulator.

name: CR2032 Coin-Cell Battery Holder
subtitle: 3V Through-Hole Coin Battery Socket
what_it_does: Holds a flat 3V CR2032 lithium coin battery for ultra-compact low-power circuits or RTC backup.
visual_tell: Small round black plastic socket with a shiny metal retention clip across the top and 2 pins underneath.
warning: Keep coin cells out of reach of children and pets.

name: FNIRSI HS-02A 100W Smart Soldering Iron
subtitle: Digital OLED USB-C PD Pen Iron
what_it_does: Heats up in seconds with precise digital temperature control (up to 100W via USB-C PD) for clean electronics soldering.
visual_tell: Sleek metallic pen-shaped soldering iron with a mini OLED temperature display, two buttons, and a USB-C port at the rear.
warning: Let the cartridge tip cool completely before swapping tips. Typical sweet spot for 60/40 leaded solder is 320–350°C.

name: FNIRSI HS02A-KU Soldering Tip
subtitle: Knife-Edge Cartridge Tip
what_it_does: Versatile knife-shaped soldering tip — use the sharp point for fine pins and the beveled flat edge for larger pads or drag soldering.
visual_tell: Long shiny silver cartridge tip with contact rings at the base and an angled knife-edge bevel at the tip.
warning: Always leave a tiny coat of fresh solder ('tinning') on the tip before turning the iron off to prevent oxidation.

name: Kurtel 60/40 Solder Wire (0.75mm, 200g)
subtitle: Sn60Pb40 RA26 3% Rosin-Core Solder
what_it_does: Creates shiny, reliable electrical and mechanical solder joints; built-in 3% flux cleans pads as it melts (~183–190°C).
visual_tell: Spool of thin, shiny silver 0.75mm solder wire labeled '60/40 Sn60Pb40'.
warning: Contains lead (Pb) — wash your hands after soldering and work in a ventilated area.

name: Lötfett Soldering Flux Paste (100g)
subtitle: Waxy Flux Tin
what_it_does: Removes surface oxidation so solder wets stubborn wires or tarnished copper pads smoothly.
visual_tell: Round metal tin containing yellowish waxy soldering paste labeled 'LÖTFETT'.
warning: Use sparingly on electronics PCBs and clean off residue with isopropyl alcohol afterward — heavy paste flux can be slightly corrosive/conductive.

name: Class ZD-180 Desoldering Wick (2mm)
subtitle: Braided Copper Solder Removal Ribbon
what_it_does: Acts like a sponge for molten solder — press it onto a joint with your hot iron to soak up excess solder or clear bridges.
visual_tell: Small plastic wheel dispensing flat, woven copper-colored braided mesh ribbon.
warning: Hold the plastic reel, not the copper braid itself — the copper conducts heat fast and will burn your fingers.

name: Xytronic 1000AS Desoldering Pump
subtitle: Anti-Static Spring Solder Sucker
what_it_does: Vacuums up blobs of molten solder instantly when desoldering through-hole pins and headers.
visual_tell: Black/silver cylindrical tube with a push-down top plunger, side trigger button, and white PTFE cone nozzle.
warning: Empty the solidified solder bits inside the barrel periodically so the plunger stays smooth.

name: Yihua YH-08C Brass Tip Cleaner
subtitle: Rosin-Coated Brass Wool Holder
what_it_does: Cleans old solder and oxidation off your hot soldering tip without thermally shocking it like a wet sponge.
visual_tell: Round dome-shaped metal holder filled with curly golden brass wool shavings.

name: Kapton High-Temp Tape (20mm)
subtitle: Polyimide Heat-Resistant Insulating Tape
what_it_does: Holds components in place while soldering and insulates bare contacts without melting near your iron.
visual_tell: Roll of glossy, translucent amber/orange tape that looks golden when unrolled.

name: UNI-T UT33D+ Digital Multimeter
subtitle: 600V 10A Handheld Diagnostic Meter
what_it_does: Measures DC/AC voltage (V), resistance (Ω — great for checking unknown resistors), current (A), and continuity (beep mode) to debug circuits.
visual_tell: Bright-red rubber holster around a dark-grey handheld meter with a backlit LCD, central rotary dial, and red/black probes.
warning: Never measure resistance (Ω) or continuity on a powered circuit, and always move the red probe back out of the 10A jack after measuring current.

name: Pro'sKit PM-737 Flush Side Cutters
subtitle: Precision Diagonal Wire Nippers
what_it_does: Cleanly trims excess component legs flush after soldering, strips/cuts hookup wire, and snaps pin headers.
visual_tell: Compact angled dark steel pliers with green and black cushioned spring-loaded handles.
warning: Only cut soft copper wire and thin component legs — cutting hard steel wire or paperclips will chip the flush jaws.

name: Pro'sKit 608-391A Helping Hands Stand
subtitle: Alligator Clip & Magnifier Soldering Holder
what_it_does: Holds PCBs, wires, and connectors rock-steady so both hands stay free for your soldering iron and solder wire.
visual_tell: Heavy black cast-iron base with adjustable chrome arms, two alligator clips, and a magnifying glass.
warning: Slide small pieces of heat-shrink tubing over the alligator clip teeth if you want to avoid scratching delicate PCBs.

name: Mano 11" Clear Organizer Box (ŞORG-11)
subtitle: Compartmentalized Storage Case
what_it_does: Keeps small sensors, LEDs, switches, and resistors separated into labeled compartments so lookalike parts never get mixed up.
visual_tell: 11-inch clear rectangular plastic organizer box with removable dividers and snap-lock latches.
notes: Tip: label slots like Mano-A1, Mano-A2, etc., and enter those codes in Pinbin's Location field.
